nodes.summary: At the BH step-up index `k`, at least `k` p-values are at most `q k / m`.
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg index satisfies the step-up condition

nodes.summary: The BH step-up index is at most `m`.
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg index is at most the number of hypotheses

nodes.summary: The Benjamini–Hochberg step-up index: the largest `k ∈ {0, …, m}` such that at least `k` p-values are at most `q k / m` (`k = 0` always qualifies).
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg step-up index

nodes.summary: The hypotheses rejected by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure at level `q`: those whose p-value is at most `q * bhIndex q p / m`.
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg rejection set

nodes.summary: The BH procedure at level `q ≥ 0` rejects exactly `bhIndex q p` hypotheses.
nodes.title: Number of Benjamini–Hochberg rejections

nodes.summary: If the p-values are independent and every true-null p-value is uniformly distributed on `[0, 1]`, the BH procedure at level `q ∈ [0, 1]` has false discovery rate at most `q |H0| / m`. Nothing is assumed about the false-null p-values beyond measurability and independence. (For `m = 0` both sides are `0`.)
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control

nodes.summary: The BH step-up index is the largest `k ≤ m` with at least `k` p-values at most `q k / m`.
nodes.title: Maximality of the Benjamini–Hochberg index

nodes.summary: At a level `q ≥ 0`, hypothesis `i` is rejected by the BH procedure exactly when replacing its p-value by `0` leaves the BH step-up index unchanged. No sign condition is imposed on the p-values.
nodes.title: Benjamini–Hochberg rejection as leave-one-out index invariance

nodes.summary: At a level `q ≥ 0`, hypothesis `i` is rejected by the BH procedure exactly when its p-value is at most `q k⁰ / m`, where `k⁰` is the BH step-up index computed after replacing the `i`-th p-value by `0`. No sign condition is imposed on the p-values.
nodes.title: Leave-one-out criterion for Benjamini–Hochberg rejection

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
